blocks.get_state:
- **{{ref:needs}}:** {{ref:needsNothing}}
- **{{ref:hints}}:** {{ref:readOnly}} · {{ref:idempotent}}

**{{ref:description}}**

```text
Get the current state of one Home Assistant entity, or of several in one call by passing a list of entity IDs. projection.kind selects compact (state plus domain-specific key attributes, the default), full, or fields with fields=[...] for exact fields (e.g. "state", "attr.brightness"). A list returns states in request order plus not_found for IDs that do not exist or are outside this access key's scope. To find entities by name, domain, area or state use search_entities; for everything about one entity, use describe_entity.
```

**{{ref:parameters}}**

```text
entity_id: string | array<string> [1..1024 items]  (required)
  Entity ID, e.g. light.living_room, or a list of entity IDs.
  - string: One entity ID, e.g. light.living_room.
  - array<string> [1..1024 items]: Several entity IDs, read in one call.
projection: object
  Output projection: compact (the default), full, or exact fields.
  kind: "compact" | "full" | "fields"  (required)
    Projection mode.
  fields: array<string>
    Exact fields; only with kind fields, and refused with compact or full.
```

**{{ref:example}}**

```json
{
  "name": "get_state",
  "arguments": {
    "entity_id": [
      "light.living_room",
      "sensor.outdoor_temperature"
    ]
  }
}
```

blocks.get_history:
- **{{ref:needs}}:** {{ref:needsNothing}}
- **{{ref:needsSometimes}}:** [{{label:caps.cap_search.label}}](guide:window.capabilities#search)
- **{{ref:hints}}:** {{ref:readOnly}} · {{ref:idempotent}}

**{{ref:description}}**

```text
Get a bounded page of Recorder history for one accessible entity. Pages run oldest first by default; set order to newest_first for the most recent changes (for example when something last happened). Defaults to state_changes, which returns attribute-free state transitions as history_csv, a CSV table with a when,state header and times in Home Assistant's local timezone to the second, and supports arbitrary time ranges. significant_states returns scrubbed full state records that Home Assistant considers significant, not every sample, and is limited to 7 days. summary returns per-state durations and entry counts instead of rows (how long a light was on, how often a pump started); a zero or total is definitive only when complete is true. Zone states are occupant counts: occupied time is the sum of counts above 0. Follow has_more with next_cursor and the same order; there is intentionally no estimated total. covered_range and data_range describe only this page; with has_more, unread_range may hold more history, so neither shows where history begins. state_changes also lists the same-state row Home Assistant records at each restart; use summary to learn whether something entered a state. In summary mode entity_id may be a list, one compact row each, or select may name them by search_entities filters instead: the way to ask which sensors entered a state in a period, in one call; with in_state only the entities that were in that state are listed, and select {} with in_state checks every entity (which went unavailable today); not_in_state lists only the entities never in those states, so which sensors did not trigger this week is not_in_state on, without reading every row. Each row names the entity and its area. With state_changes, an entity_id list returns each entity's own page in one call (limit and order apply per entity; continue one alone with its next_cursor). A state's last_entered is when it last began, such as when someone last arrived home; a row with recorded_from has no record before that time, so a state held since then began then or earlier. Entities past what one result holds are named in not_summarized. With attribute, summary totals that attribute's values instead of the state, such as how long each thermostat's hvac_action was heating or cooling.
```

**{{ref:parameters}}**

```text
entity_id: string | array<string> [1..500 items]
  Entity ID, or in summary or state_changes mode a list of entity IDs.
  - string: Accessible entity whose Recorder history to read.
  - array<string> [1..500 items]: Several entities, in summary or state_changes mode.
start_time: string
  ISO timestamp or relative string (30min, 24h, 7d, 2w, 1mo). Defaults to 24h before end_time.
end_time: string
  ISO timestamp or relative string. Defaults to now.
mode: "state_changes" | "significant_states" | "summary"  (default "state_changes")
  state_changes: state transitions as a CSV table. significant_states: scrubbed significant state records. summary: per-state totals; omit limit and order.
attribute: string [..255 chars]
  summary only: total this attribute's values (e.g. hvac_action) instead of the state, over at most 7 days. Values read as in significant_states; a sensitive attribute reads as absent, so its rows count under the state.
limit: integer [1..1000]  (default 100)
  Maximum rows in this page: the earliest in the range, or the latest with order newest_first.
order: "oldest_first" | "newest_first"  (default "oldest_first")
  oldest_first pages forward from start_time; newest_first pages backward from end_time.
cursor: string
  The ISO UTC next_cursor from the previous page.
select: object
  Summary mode, instead of entity_id: summarize the entities these search_entities filters match (diagnostic and configuration entities only with include_diagnostic). With in_state or not_in_state, an empty select scans every accessible entity.
  query: string
    Words matched against entity_id, name and aliases.
  domain: string | array<string>
    One or more domains.
  device_class: string | array<string>
    One or more device classes.
  integration: string | array<string>
    One or more providing integrations.
  radio: "zigbee" | "zwave" | "matter" | "bluetooth" | array<("zigbee" | "zwave" | "matter" | "bluetooth")>
    How the device connects.
  power: "battery"
    battery: devices whose battery level or low battery is a diagnostic reading.
  area: string
    An area or floor.
  include_diagnostic: boolean
    Also summarize diagnostic and configuration entities.
in_state: string | array<string> [1.. items]
  Summary of several entities only: keep the entities that were in one of these states at some point in the range, e.g. unavailable; the rest are only counted in scanned.
not_in_state: string | array<string> [1.. items]
  Summary of several entities only: keep the entities never in any of these states in the range, including at its start, e.g. on for sensors that did not trigger; the rest are only counted in scanned. Not with in_state.
```

**{{ref:example}}**

```json
{
  "name": "get_history",
  "arguments": {
    "entity_id": "binary_sensor.front_door",
    "start_time": "7d",
    "mode": "summary"
  }
}
```
blocks.get_statistics:
- **{{ref:needs}}:** {{ref:needsNothing}}

- **{{ref:hints}}:** {{ref:readOnly}} · {{ref:idempotent}}

**{{ref:description}}**

```text
Get a bounded page of Recorder statistics for one accessible entity. Five-minute data uses short-term retention; hour, day, week, month, and year use long-term statistics. Calendar periods align in Home Assistant's local timezone. Rows come as statistics_csv, a CSV table with a header: start in local time (a row ends where the next starts), then the values in units, rounded to keep at least 4 significant digits; an empty cell has no value. Follow has_more with next_cursor; there is intentionally no estimated total. For individual state changes use get_history. A list of entity_id, or select with search_entities filters, returns one row per entity for the whole window instead: mean, min and max of a measurement, change of a total, in its unit. That is the way to compare sensors (warmest room, most energy used) in one call.
```

**{{ref:parameters}}**

```text
entity_id: string | array<string> [1..500 items]
  Entity ID, or a list of entity IDs.
  - string: Accessible entity whose Recorder statistics to read.
  - array<string> [1..500 items]: Several entities, one row each for the whole window.
select: object
  Instead of entity_id: one row for the whole window per entity these search_entities filters match (diagnostic and configuration entities only with include_diagnostic).
  query: string
    Words matched against entity_id, name and aliases.
  domain: string | array<string>
    One or more domains.
  device_class: string | array<string>
    One or more device classes.
  integration: string | array<string>
    One or more providing integrations.
  radio: "zigbee" | "zwave" | "matter" | "bluetooth" | array<("zigbee" | "zwave" | "matter" | "bluetooth")>
    How the device connects.
  power: "battery"
    battery: devices whose battery level or low battery is a diagnostic reading.
  area: string
    An area or floor.
  include_diagnostic: boolean
    Also summarize diagnostic and configuration entities.
start_time: string
  ISO or relative time. Defaults to 30 days before end_time.
end_time: string
  ISO or relative time. Defaults to now.
period: "5minute" | "hour" | "day" | "week" | "month" | "year"  (default "hour")
  Aggregation period, aligned to Home Assistant's local calendar.
statistic_types: array<("mean" | "min" | "max" | "sum" | "state" | "change" | "last_reset")> [1.. items]
  Subset of the statistics fields to return.
limit: integer [1..1000]  (default 100)
  Requested page size, counted from the start of the range. Safe per-period caps can lower effective_limit.
cursor: string
  The ISO UTC next_cursor from the previous page.
```

**{{ref:example}}**

```json
{
  "name": "get_statistics",
  "arguments": {
    "entity_id": "sensor.outdoor_temperature",

**{{ref:description}}**

```text
Create one event on a writable calendar. Integration feature checks, MESA and approval apply, and the result is a durable recovery receipt. For a recurring event set event.rrule without the RRULE: prefix, e.g. FREQ=WEEKLY;BYDAY=MO,WE or FREQ=MONTHLY;BYMONTHDAY=1. No automatic retry or rollback; if a write is interrupted, read get_calendar_write before trying again.
```

**{{ref:parameters}}**

```text
entity_id: string  (required)
  A calendar.* entity ID.
event: object  (required)
  Event fields for creation or the chosen update mode.
  summary: string  (required)
    Event title.
  start: string  (required)
    ISO date for all-day events or ISO timestamp with timezone.
  end: string  (required)
    Exclusive end; same date/time type as start.
  description: string
    Event description.
  location: string
    Event location.
  rrule: string
    Recurrence rule without the RRULE: prefix, e.g. FREQ=WEEKLY;BYDAY=MO or FREQ=DAILY;COUNT=5; daily, weekly, monthly and yearly rules are supported.
```

**{{ref:example}}**

```json
{
  "name": "create_calendar_event",
  "arguments": {
    "entity_id": "calendar.family",
    "event": {
      "summary": "Bin day",
      "start": "2026-11-23",
      "end": "2026-11-24",
      "rrule": "FREQ=WEEKLY;BYDAY=MO"
    }
  }
}
```
blocks.update_calendar_event:
- **{{ref:needs}}:** [{{label:caps.cap_calendar_write.label}}](guide:window.capabilities#calendar-write)
- **{{ref:hints}}:** {{ref:changes}} · {{ref:destructive}}
- **{{ref:onConfirm}}:** {{ref:confirmApproval}}

**{{ref:description}}**

```text
Update one event addressed by its current uid and content_hash from get_calendar_events. For a recurring event pick one occurrence with recurrence_id, optionally with recurrence_range THISANDFUTURE; the whole series is never backed up or rewritten. Same checks and receipt as create_calendar_event.
```

**{{ref:parameters}}**

```text
entity_id: string  (required)
  A calendar.* entity ID.
uid: string  (required)
  Exact integration UID from get_calendar_events.
start_time: string  (required)
  ISO date or timestamp locating the current occurrence; window at most 31 days.
end_time: string  (required)
  Exclusive end of current occurrence lookup window.
expected_hash: string  (required)
  Current occurrence content_hash from get_calendar_events.
recurrence_id: string
  Exact occurrence ID from readback; required for recurring writes.
recurrence_range: "THISANDFUTURE"
  Apply to this and future occurrences. Requires recurrence_id and a visible rrule; edited exceptions are refused. Prior snapshot does not cover the whole series.
event: object  (required)
  Event fields for creation or the chosen update mode.
  summary: string
    Event title.
  start: string
    ISO date for all-day events or ISO timestamp with timezone.
  end: string
    Exclusive end; same date/time type as start.
  description: string | null
    Event description.
  location: string | null
    Event location.
  rrule: string
    Recurrence rule without the RRULE: prefix, e.g. FREQ=WEEKLY;BYDAY=MO or FREQ=DAILY;COUNT=5; daily, weekly, monthly and yearly rules are supported.
mode: "replace" | "patch"  (required)
  replace requires summary/start/end and clears omitted optional fields; patch preserves omissions and accepts null to clear description/location/rrule.
```

**{{ref:example}}**

```json
{
  "name": "update_calendar_event",
  "arguments": {
    "entity_id": "calendar.family",
    "uid": "4f1c2a90-6d1e-4b7a-9a52-0c3d7e1b2f44",
    "start_time": "2026-11-23",
    "end_time": "2026-11-24",
    "expected_hash": "9b2e5c1a7d3f4e60",

    "event": {
      "location": "Kerb outside"
    }
  }
}
```

blocks.set_todo_item:
- **{{ref:needs}}:** {{ref:needsNothing}}
- **{{ref:hints}}:** {{ref:changes}} · {{ref:destructive}}

**{{ref:description}}**

```text
Add, update or remove one item on a todo list the access key can WRITE, or clear its completed items. add takes summary (the item's text) and optional due and description. update renames (summary), completes or reopens (status), or sets due or description of the item named by item: its uid from get_todo_items, or its exact summary when only one item has it; null clears due or description, and cleared gives the old values. A null in summary or status marks a padded call: its other nulls are ignored and listed in ignored_null. remove deletes that item. clear_completed takes only the list: it reads the completed items and removes exactly those, by uid, up to 500 in one call and only as many as the result can name; removed gives each uid and summary, remaining_completed what is left. Removal is permanent: nothing can restore an item. Runs as the todo service through call_service, with the same scope, MESA and approval checks, then reads the list back: the result gives the item as the list now holds it and verified; a change that does not read back is an error. An approved remove or clear leaves any item changed since the review, listed in not_removed; an approved add or update answers as call_service does.
```

**{{ref:parameters}}**

```text
entity_id: string  (required)
  The todo.* entity ID of the list.
action: "add" | "update" | "remove" | "clear_completed"  (required)
  What to do.
item: string
  update and remove: the item's uid, or its exact summary.
summary: string [..1000 chars]
  add: the item's text. update: its new text.
status: "needs_action" | "completed"
  update: completed or needs_action.
due: string | null
  A date (2026-11-02) or a date and time (2026-11-02T18:00), in Home Assistant's local time when no offset is given. update: null clears it.
description: string | null [..4000 chars]
  A longer note on the item, where the list supports one. update: null clears it.
```

**{{ref:example}}**

```json
{
  "name": "set_todo_item",
  "arguments": {
    "entity_id": "todo.shopping_list",
    "action": "add",
    "summary": "Milk"
  }
}
```

blocks.call_service:
- **{{ref:needs}}:** {{ref:needsNothing}}
- **{{ref:needsSometimes}}:** [{{label:caps.cap_physical_control.label}}](guide:window.capabilities#physical-control), [{{label:caps.cap_notify.label}}](guide:window.capabilities#notify), [{{label:caps.cap_broadcast.label}}](guide:window.capabilities#broadcast), [{{label:caps.cap_service_response.label}}](guide:window.capabilities#service-response), [{{label:caps.cap_camera_read.label}}](guide:window.capabilities#camera-read), [{{label:caps.cap_restart.label}}](guide:window.capabilities#restart), [{{label:caps.cap_yaml_edit.label}}](guide:window.capabilities#yaml-edit), [{{label:caps.cap_scene_write.label}}](guide:window.capabilities#scene-write), [{{label:caps.cap_registry_write.label}}](guide:window.capabilities#registry-write), [{{label:caps.cap_esphome_flash.label}}](guide:window.capabilities#esphome-flash)
- **{{ref:hints}}:** {{ref:changes}} · {{ref:destructive}}

**{{ref:description}}**

```text
Call a Home Assistant service. Target groups (kind entity, device, area or all) are resolved and flattened to the entities this access key can write; out-of-scope targets are dropped silently. A service only takes the targets it declares: every target must be of the service's own domain or listed in its description, and homeassistant.turn_on, turn_off, toggle and update_entity take any entity, without data when a target is a script. A service without a target is refused, except the core reloads (cap_yaml_edit), homeassistant.restart and stop (cap_restart), ESPHome device actions (write on everything the device can operate, and MESA over all its entities) and the Music Assistant library reads music_assistant.search and get_library (cap_service_response and read on a Music Assistant entity; for a genre, mood or year search playlists first; with none, search for artists that fit and pass the found uris as the music_assistant.play_media media_id list). The call passes the capability gate and per-entity MESA policy, so it may return pending_approval or be refused. Preview a risky call first with dry_run_service (and whatif to see which automations it would trigger). For runtime controls use automation.trigger (run actions, skip_condition defaults true), automation.turn_on/turn_off (enable/disable future triggers; turn_off also stops actions unless stop_actions=false), script.turn_on (start, inputs in data.variables), script.turn_off (stop all runs), or scene.turn_on (activate). Named script services require the exact script entity target and wait for completion; their inputs go directly in data. An entity named in a script or automation input needs the same access as a target. Use create/edit tools for configuration and set_entity for registry disabling. The result's targets reports how many entities were called, each one's state right after the call, and any that were unavailable, which Home Assistant skips without failing the call. Use find_available_actions with include_fields to learn a service's data fields first.
```

**{{ref:parameters}}**

```text
service: object  (required)
  Service to execute.
  domain: string  (required)
    Service domain.
  name: string  (required)
    Service name.
  data: object
    Additional service data without target selectors; selectors here are refused.
targets: array<object> [1..32 items]
  Explicit target groups required for supported calls; use kind all for intentional domain-wide targeting.
  each item:
    kind: "entity" | "device" | "area" | "all"  (required)
      Target selector kind.
    ids: array<string> [1..1024 items]
      IDs for entity, device, or area targets; an area may also be named by its name or an alias.
```

**{{ref:example}}**

```json
{
  "name": "call_service",
  "arguments": {
    "service": {
      "domain": "light",
      "name": "turn_on",
      "data": {
        "brightness_pct": 60
      }
    },
    "targets": [
      {
        "kind": "area",
        "ids": [
          "living_room"
        ]
      }
    ]
  }
}
```
blocks.get_audit_summary:
- **{{ref:needs}}:** {{ref:needsNothing}}
- **{{ref:hints}}:** {{ref:readOnly}} · {{ref:idempotent}}
- **{{ref:household}}:** {{ref:householdAdmin}}

**{{ref:description}}**

```text
Return this access key's own recent activity from the Phoenix MCP audit log (request_id, time, method, resource, outcome), newest first. Only this access key's entries are returned. Useful for self-correction (did my last call succeed?). A call refused because an entity is outside this key's scope is listed as not_found, as it was answered. No capability required.
```

**{{ref:parameters}}**

```text
limit: integer [1..200]  (default 50)
  Maximum recent audit entries to return.
outcome: string

**{{ref:description}}**

```text
Read the Energy dashboard configuration: which statistics are registered as grid, solar, battery, gas or water sources, and which appear as individual devices. Home Assistant records this nowhere else, so call it before removing an integration or deleting an energy sensor to see whether the Energy dashboard depends on it; referenced_entities lists every entity the configuration points at. configured is false when Energy was never set up. With start_time or end_time it also returns usage: how much each source measured (grid imported and exported, solar produced, battery discharged and charged, gas and water used) and each device consumed in that range, plus electricity_used, the home's use as the Energy dashboard sums it, so how much energy the house or each device used is this one call. Read-only: this cannot change the Energy dashboard.
```

**{{ref:parameters}}**

```text
start_time: string
  ISO timestamp or relative string (24h, 7d); adds usage from then. Defaults to 24h before end_time.
end_time: string
  ISO timestamp or relative string; adds usage until then. Defaults to now.
```

blocks.edit_energy_config:
- **{{ref:needs}}:** [{{label:caps.cap_energy_write.label}}](guide:window.capabilities#energy-write)
- **{{ref:hints}}:** {{ref:changes}} · {{ref:destructive}} · {{ref:idempotent}}
- **{{ref:onConfirm}}:** {{ref:confirmApproval}}

**{{ref:description}}**

```text
Change one addressed part of the Energy dashboard. This never takes a whole configuration: Home Assistant replaces a whole list at a time, so sending one would delete every entry you did not resend. Pick an op. 'replace_statistic' points an existing entry at a different statistic, everywhere it appears; address the old one with statistic, or with device_name when get_energy_config showed it as <redacted> (a dead entry has no usable id, and the name is the only handle left). 'add_device' starts tracking statistic as an individual device, with an optional name. 'remove_device' drops one entry, addressed the same two ways. 'rename_device' changes the label on an existing entry. 'remove_source' drops the source named by source_type, and refuses when there is more than one of that type rather than guessing which. 'set_source' updates the grid, solar, battery, gas or water source named by source_type, creating it if there is none. It cannot add a second source of a type, and refuses when there is already more than one rather than guessing which. It sets only the fields you pass: stat_energy_from and stat_energy_to (grid import/export, battery discharge/charge), number_energy_price and number_energy_price_export. Call get_energy_config first to see what is there. A verified write returns a recovery_id for restore_configuration, and issues: Home Assistant's own check of the saved setup, such as a statistic with the wrong unit (null when the check could not run).
```

**{{ref:parameters}}**

```text
operation: "replace_statistic" | "add_device" | "remove_device" | "rename_device" | "set_source" | "remove_source"  (required)
  Which addressed Energy change to make.
target: object  (required)
  The existing statistic, redacted device name, or Energy source addressed by the operation.
  kind: "statistic" | "device_name" | "source"  (required)
    Address kind.
  id: string
    Statistic ID.
  name: string
    Device display name.
  source_type: "grid" | "solar" | "battery" | "gas" | "water"
    Energy source kind.
changes: object  (required)
  Fields changed by the selected operation. Empty for a removal.
  new_statistic: string
    Replacement statistic.
  name: string
    Device display name.
  stat_energy_from: string | null
    For set_source: grid import, solar production, battery discharge, or the gas/water meter.
  stat_energy_to: string | null
    For set_source: grid export or battery charge. Not accepted on solar, gas or water.
  number_energy_price: number | null
    For set_source: a fixed price per unit consumed. Grid, gas and water only.
  number_energy_price_export: number | null
    For set_source: a fixed price per unit exported. Grid only.
  entity_energy_price: string | null
    For set_source: an entity publishing the current price per unit, for a time-of-use tariff. Use instead of number_energy_price. Grid, gas and water only.
  entity_energy_price_export: string | null
    For set_source: an entity publishing the current export price. Grid only.
  stat_cost: string | null
    For set_source: an existing cost statistic to use instead of letting Home Assistant derive cost from a price. Grid, gas and water only.
  stat_compensation: string | null
    For set_source: an existing statistic of export compensation received. Grid only.
```

**{{ref:example}}**

```json
{
  "name": "edit_energy_config",
  "arguments": {
    "operation": "replace_statistic",
    "target": {
      "kind": "statistic",
      "id": "sensor.old_power_meter_energy"
    },
    "changes": {
      "new_statistic": "sensor.new_power_meter_energy"
    }
  }
}
```

blocks.get_logs:
- **{{ref:needs}}:** [{{label:caps.cap_log_read.label}}](guide:window.capabilities#log-read)
- **{{ref:needsWhen}} `source: fault_log`:** [{{label:caps.cap_diagnostics.label}}](guide:window.capabilities#diagnostics)
- **{{ref:needsWhen}} `source: integration_debug`:** [{{label:caps.cap_diagnostics.label}}](guide:window.capabilities#diagnostics)
- **{{ref:hints}}:** {{ref:readOnly}} · {{ref:idempotent}}

**{{ref:description}}**

```text
Read Home Assistant's bounded, deduplicated WARNING-and-above system-log ring, newest first. Phoenix MCP's own records are excluded. The response reports source status and coverage, effective filters, compact message/traceback previews with truncation metadata, and stateless cursor pagination. This is not a continuous raw log: repeated records share one bucket and live bucket updates can move records between pages. Search matches full scrubbed text before compaction. Response byte limits can return fewer buckets than limit; continue with next_cursor. Pass a bucket's detail_ref to get_log_detail for its full scrubbed text. Set source=integration_debug to read the INFO and DEBUG records of integrations this access key raised with set_integration_log_level, written while it held the raise (Home Assistant's system log never keeps them; other keys' raises are not readable); it also requires Diagnostics and accepts integration, search, limit and cursor. Set source=fault_log for a protected bounded tail of home-assistant.log.fault, requiring both Log read and Diagnostics. Fault dumps preserve all thread lines within each block, support scrubbed search, block order and whole-block cursor paging, and report incomplete coverage. They have no timestamps or log levels; absent/empty differs from unreadable.
```

**{{ref:parameters}}**

```text
source: "system_log" | "fault_log" | "integration_debug"  (default "system_log")
  system_log reads the HA ring; fault_log reads native fault dumps; integration_debug reads captured INFO/DEBUG records. fault_log and integration_debug also require Diagnostics.
order: "newest_first" | "oldest_first"
  fault_log only. Order whole dumps; defaults to newest_first. Lines inside each dump stay in original order.
level: "WARNING" | "ERROR"
  system_log only. Minimum log level. WARNING returns WARNING+ERROR; ERROR returns ERROR only. Defaults to WARNING. Home Assistant's system log holds WARNING and above only, so INFO and DEBUG entries never enter it; read those with source integration_debug. Asking for INFO or DEBUG here is an error rather than a WARNING result.
integration: string [..512 chars]
  system_log and integration_debug. Optional integration name to filter by (e.g. 'hue', 'mqtt'). Matches homeassistant.components.<name> and custom_components.<name>.
logger: string [..512 chars]
  system_log only. Optional exact logger-name prefix, e.g. homeassistant.components.zha.
search: string [..512 chars]
  Case-insensitive literal search after scrubbing; fault_log matches whole blocks and preserves every line.
since: string
  system_log only. Optional ISO timestamp or relative time. Filters by each bucket's latest occurrence.
until: string
  system_log only. Optional ISO timestamp or relative time. Filters by each bucket's latest occurrence.
limit: integer [1..100]
  Maximum entries (1-100): system_log buckets default 50; fault_log whole blocks default 10, also bounded by response bytes.
cursor: string
  Opaque next_cursor from the previous page. Reuse the same filters.
```

**{{ref:example}}**

```json
{
  "name": "get_logs",
  "arguments": {
    "level": "ERROR",
    "integration": "mqtt",
    "since": "24h"
  }
}
```
blocks.get_phoenix_diagnostics:
- **{{ref:needs}}:** [{{label:caps.cap_diagnostics.label}}](guide:window.capabilities#diagnostics), [{{label:caps.cap_log_read.label}}](guide:window.capabilities#log-read)
- **{{ref:hints}}:** {{ref:readOnly}} · {{ref:idempotent}}

**{{ref:description}}**

```text
Read Phoenix MCP's own retained WARNING-and-above diagnostic buckets with stronger redaction for credentials, topology, paths, opaque identifiers, and inaccessible entities. Uses the same bounded source-status, coverage, filter, and cursor contract as get_logs, including compact previews, explicit truncation, full scrubbed search, byte-bounded pages and access-key-bound detail_ref values for get_log_detail. Requires both Diagnostics and Log read capabilities.
```

**{{ref:parameters}}**

```text
level: "WARNING" | "ERROR"  (default "WARNING")
  Minimum retained level. WARNING returns WARNING+ERROR; ERROR returns ERROR only.
logger: string [..512 chars]
  Optional Phoenix logger namespace prefix, e.g. custom_components.phoenix_mcp.mcp_transport.
search: string [..512 chars]
  Case-insensitive literal search applied only after the stronger Phoenix diagnostic scrub.
since: string
  Optional ISO timestamp or relative time. Filters by latest occurrence.
until: string
  Optional ISO timestamp or relative time. Filters by latest occurrence.
limit: integer [1..100]  (default 50)
  Maximum Phoenix diagnostic buckets to return.
cursor: string
  Opaque next_cursor from the previous page. Reuse the same filters.
```

**{{ref:example}}**

```json
{
  "name": "get_phoenix_diagnostics",
  "arguments": {
    "level": "ERROR",
    "since": "24h"
  }
}
```
blocks.get_log_detail:
- **{{ref:needs}}:** [{{label:caps.cap_log_read.label}}](guide:window.capabilities#log-read)
- **{{ref:needsSometimes}}:** [{{label:caps.cap_diagnostics.label}}](guide:window.capabilities#diagnostics)
- **{{ref:hints}}:** {{ref:readOnly}} · {{ref:idempotent}}

**{{ref:description}}**

```text
Fetch one bounded, scrubbed text chunk of a log bucket returned by get_logs (system_log) or get_phoenix_diagnostics, by the bucket's detail_ref. A reference works only for the access key that received it and only while the bucket is unchanged; a stale one needs a fresh query. Continue long text with detail.next_offset while detail.has_more is true.
```

**{{ref:parameters}}**

```text
detail_ref: string pattern ^[0-9a-f]{64}$  (required)
  The detail_ref of one bucket from get_logs or get_phoenix_diagnostics.
detail_field: "message" | "exception"  (default "message")
  message for a retained message variant, exception for the traceback.
message_index: integer [0..]
  Message detail only; omit for exception. Zero-based retained variant index in the bucket, 0 when omitted.
detail_offset: integer [0..]  (default 0)
  Character offset in the full scrubbed text. Continue with detail.next_offset; detail.has_more reports remaining text.
```

**{{ref:example}}**

```json
{
  "name": "get_log_detail",
  "arguments": {
    "detail_ref": "5d0c9a7e3b1f42c6a8e4d2b07f9c13a5e6b8d0f2c4a6e8b0d2f4a6c8e0b2d4f6",
    "detail_field": "exception"
  }
}
```
blocks.get_logbook:
- **{{ref:needs}}:** [{{label:caps.cap_log_read.label}}](guide:window.capabilities#log-read)
- **{{ref:hints}}:** {{ref:readOnly}} · {{ref:idempotent}}

**{{ref:description}}**

```text
Read the human-readable Home Assistant logbook in chronological order. Narrow by up to 100 accessible entities and up to 100 accessible devices, or by one causal context_id. Home-wide queries are limited to 7 days and resource- or context-narrowed queries to 31 days. The response reports the post-permission, post-search total before limiting and whether the most-recent slice is truncated; when it is, pass older_end_time as end_time with the same start_time to read the earlier entries. This is narrative event history; get_logs is the system error log, and get_history is raw state history.
```

**{{ref:parameters}}**

```text
start_time: string
  ISO timestamp or relative string (24h, 7d, 2w). Defaults to 24h before now, also when end_time is given.
end_time: string
  ISO timestamp or relative string. Defaults to now.
target: object
  Optional resource or causal-context filter.
  kind: "resources" | "context"  (required)
    Filter mode.
  id: string
    Context ULID when kind is context.
  entity_ids: array<string>
    Entity IDs when kind is resources; at most 100 unique values, with duplicates normalized.
  device_ids: array<string>
    Device registry IDs when kind is resources; at most 100 unique values, with duplicates normalized.
search: string [..512 chars]
  Case-insensitive literal search over safe name, message, and state fields after permission filtering and redaction. Does not widen the allowed time range.
limit: integer [1..1000]  (default 100)
  Maximum entries to return (1-1000, default 100). The most recent matching entries are kept and returned chronologically.
```

**{{ref:example}}**

```json
{
  "name": "get_logbook",
  "arguments": {
    "start_time": "24h",
    "target": {
      "kind": "resources",
      "entity_ids": [
        "lock.front_door"
      ]
    }
  }
}
```
blocks.set_integration_log_level:

- **{{ref:needs}}:** [{{label:caps.cap_blueprint_write.label}}](guide:window.capabilities#blueprint-write)
- **{{ref:needsSometimes}}:** [{{label:caps.cap_automation_write.label}}](guide:window.capabilities#automation-write), [{{label:caps.cap_script_write.label}}](guide:window.capabilities#script-write)
- **{{ref:hints}}:** {{ref:changes}}
- **{{ref:onConfirm}}:** {{ref:confirmApproval}}

**{{ref:description}}**

```text
Create a NEW blueprint from YAML you supply. Use this to author a reusable pattern once and instantiate it many times with create_automation's use_blueprint. content must be a complete blueprint document: a top-level 'blueprint:' block with name/domain/input, plus the triggers/conditions/actions (or sequence, for a script blueprint) that reference those inputs with !input. Fails if the path already exists; use edit_blueprint to replace one. There is no import-from-URL: if you have a URL, fetch it yourself and pass the YAML here, so the operator reviews the actual source. May require admin approval. A verified write returns a recovery_id for restore_configuration.
```

**{{ref:parameters}}**

```text
domain: "automation" | "script"  (required)
  Which kind of blueprint this is. Must match the domain declared inside the content.
path: string  (required)
  Relative path within the domain's blueprint folder, e.g. 'my_author/motion_light.yaml'. A .yaml suffix is added if omitted.
content: string  (required)
  The complete blueprint YAML document.
```

{
  "name": "create_blueprint",
  "arguments": {
    "domain": "automation",
    "path": "my_author/door_left_open.yaml",
    "content": "blueprint:\n  name: Door left open\n  domain: automation\n  input:\n    door:\n      selector:\n        entity:\n          domain: binary_sensor\ntriggers:\n  - trigger: state\n    entity_id: !input door\n    to: \"on\"\n    for: \"00:10:00\"\nactions:\n  - action: persistent_notification.create\n    data:\n      message: The door is still open.\n"
  }
}
```
blocks.edit_blueprint:
- **{{ref:needs}}:** [{{label:caps.cap_blueprint_write.label}}](guide:window.capabilities#blueprint-write)
- **{{ref:needsSometimes}}:** [{{label:caps.cap_automation_write.label}}](guide:window.capabilities#automation-write), [{{label:caps.cap_script_write.label}}](guide:window.capabilities#script-write)
- **{{ref:hints}}:** {{ref:changes}} · {{ref:destructive}} · {{ref:idempotent}}
- **{{ref:onConfirm}}:** {{ref:confirmApproval}}

**{{ref:description}}**

```text
Replace an EXISTING blueprint's YAML (a full-document replace; preserve any part you are not changing). High blast radius: Home Assistant immediately reloads every automation or script built from this blueprint, and those entities' own configs do not change, so the effect is invisible in their history. Read the current source with get_blueprint first, and prefer editing the individual automation when only one of them needs to differ. May require admin approval; the approval names the entities that will be reloaded. A verified write returns a recovery_id for restore_configuration.
```

**{{ref:parameters}}**

```text
domain: "automation" | "script"  (required)
  The blueprint's domain, as returned by list_blueprints.
path: string  (required)
  The blueprint path exactly as returned by list_blueprints.
content: string  (required)
  The complete replacement blueprint YAML document.
```

**{{ref:example}}**

```json
{
  "name": "edit_blueprint",
  "arguments": {
    "domain": "automation",
    "path": "my_author/door_left_open.yaml",
    "content": "blueprint:\n  name: Door left open\n  domain: automation\n  input:\n    door:\n      selector:\n        entity:\n          domain: binary_sensor\ntriggers:\n  - trigger: state\n    entity_id: !input door\n    to: \"on\"\n    for: \"00:05:00\"\nactions:\n  - action: persistent_notification.create\n    data:\n      message: The door is still open.\n"
  }
}
```

blocks.set_entity:
- **{{ref:needs}}:** [{{label:caps.cap_registry_write.label}}](guide:window.capabilities#registry-write)
- **{{ref:hints}}:** {{ref:changes}} · {{ref:destructive}} · {{ref:idempotent}}
- **{{ref:onConfirm}}:** {{ref:confirmApproval}}

**{{ref:description}}**

```text
Update an entity's user-controlled registry metadata: friendly name, icon, area, device class, enabled/hidden state, labels, categories, and/or the alternative spoken names (aliases) Assist matches it by. Requires WRITE access to a live entity; a disabled or otherwise registry-only entity instead requires inherited WRITE on its device or domain. cap_registry_write also applies and is often admin-confirmed. Use null to clear name, icon, area_id, or device_class. Aliases and labels are edited by adding and removing values rather than by replacing the list, so an entity never loses the ability to answer to its own name; describe_entity reports the names it currently matches. new_entity_id renames within the same domain only after checking Phoenix identity blockers and showing known relationship consumers. Rename is governed by the fully inherited MESA profile. Captured in version history. Registry disabling unloads an entity; to stop running script executions use call_service with script.turn_off. To disable future automation triggers use automation.turn_off.
```

**{{ref:parameters}}**

```text
entity_id: string  (required)
  Entity registry ID to update.
changes: object  (required)
  User-controlled metadata changes.
  name: string | null
    The entity's own name, not its whole shown name: from Home Assistant 2026.11 an entity on a device shows as the device name followed by this, so send 'Temperature', not 'Kitchen Sensor Temperature'. Earlier releases show this alone. The approval preview and the result give composed_name, the name it produces. null or an empty string restores the integration-provided name. Non-empty names cannot contain only quotes and whitespace.
  use_device_name: boolean
    true names the entity after its device, following renames (Home Assistant 2026.10+, named device); false restores the integration name. Not with name.
  icon: string | null
    New icon, or null to clear it.
  area_id: string | null
    Area assignment, or null to clear it.
  device_class: string | null
    User device-class override, or null to clear it.
  new_entity_id: string
    New same-domain entity ID.
  enabled: boolean
    Enable or user-disable the entity.
  hidden: boolean
    Set user-hidden state.
  add_aliases: string | array<string>
    One alias or an array of aliases to add.
  remove_aliases: string | array<string>
    One alias or an array of aliases to remove.
  add_labels: array<string>
    Label IDs to add.
  remove_labels: array<string>
    Label IDs to remove.
  categories: object<string, string | null>
    Category patch keyed by scope. Values are existing category IDs; null removes that scope.
```

**{{ref:example}}**

```json
{
  "name": "set_entity",
  "arguments": {
    "entity_id": "sensor.power_meter",
    "changes": {
      "name": "Power",
      "add_aliases": [
        "mains power"
      ]
    }
  }
}
```
blocks.set_area_or_floor:
- **{{ref:needs}}:** [{{label:caps.cap_registry_write.label}}](guide:window.capabilities#registry-write)
- **{{ref:hints}}:** {{ref:changes}} · {{ref:destructive}}
- **{{ref:onConfirm}}:** {{ref:confirmApproval}}

**{{ref:description}}**

```text
Create, update or delete an area or floor through cap_registry_write. Scoped access keys require WRITE on every affected registry entity and an explicit WRITE grant on every affected device; empty locations and creation require pass-through authority. Use exact IDs from list_areas/list_floors. Area labels must reference existing label IDs: labels replaces the set ([] clears), while add_labels/remove_labels patch it. Floors have no labels. Deletion clears placement references, does not rewrite consumers, and cannot be restored automatically. Approvals refuse identity, membership, metadata or MESA drift. Inspect current state after an interrupted write before retrying.
```

**{{ref:parameters}}**

```text
kind: "area" | "floor"  (required)
  Location registry to change.
operation: "create" | "update" | "delete"  (required)
  Explicit lifecycle operation.
location_id: string
  Exact existing ID for update/delete; omit for create.
changes: object
  Required for create/update; omit for delete. Creation requires name.
  name: string
    Location name.
  icon: string | null
    Icon, or null to clear.
  aliases: array<string>
    Replace aliases; [] clears.
  floor_id: string | null
    Area only: writable destination floor, or null to clear.
  level: integer | null
    Floor only: floor level, or null to clear.
  labels: array<string>
    Area only: replace labels with existing IDs; [] clears. Cannot combine with label patches.
  add_labels: array<string>
    Area only: add existing label IDs, preserving other labels.
  remove_labels: array<string>
    Area only: remove existing label IDs, preserving other labels.
```

**{{ref:example}}**

```json
{
  "name": "set_area_or_floor",
  "arguments": {
    "kind": "area",
    "operation": "update",
    "location_id": "workshop",
    "changes": {
      "floor_id": "ground_floor"
    }
  }
}
```
blocks.set_device:
- **{{ref:needs}}:** [{{label:caps.cap_registry_write.label}}](guide:window.capabilities#registry-write)
- **{{ref:hints}}:** {{ref:changes}} · {{ref:destructive}} · {{ref:idempotent}}
- **{{ref:onConfirm}}:** {{ref:confirmApproval}}

**{{ref:description}}**

```text
Update one device's user-controlled registry metadata: display-name override, area, enabled state, and labels. Requires cap_registry_write plus an explicit WRITE grant on the device; attached entity or domain grants cannot authorize a whole-device mutation. Use changes.name: null to restore the integration-provided name, or area_id: null to clear placement. Renaming a device keeps its entities' entity_ids; entities named relative to the device show the new name in their friendly names. Change an entity_id with set_entity. Only user-disabled devices may be toggled, and a disabled owning config entry prevents enable. Name, area, and enabled-state changes require every attached registry entity to remain writable; label-only edits do not. Device rename and enable/disable are evaluated against every attached entity's fully inherited MESA profile and may be blocked or merged into the normal approval. Captured in version history.
```

**{{ref:parameters}}**

```text
device_id: string  (required)
  The device registry id.
changes: object  (required)
  User-controlled device metadata changes.
  name: string | null
    Display-name override; null restores the integration-provided name. Non-empty names cannot contain only quotes and whitespace.
  area_id: string | null
    Area assignment.
  enabled: boolean
    Enabled state.
  add_labels: array<string>
    Label IDs to add.
  remove_labels: array<string>
    Label IDs to remove.
```

**{{ref:example}}**

```json
{
  "name": "set_device",
  "arguments": {
    "device_id": "8f3c1a2b4d5e6f708192a3b4c5d6e7f8",
    "changes": {
      "area_id": "kitchen"
    }
  }
}
```
blocks.remove_device:
- **{{ref:needs}}:** [{{label:caps.cap_integration_write.label}}](guide:window.capabilities#integration-write)
- **{{ref:hints}}:** {{ref:changes}} · {{ref:destructive}} · {{ref:idempotent}}
- **{{ref:onConfirm}}:** {{ref:confirmApproval}}

**{{ref:description}}**

```text
Ask one owning integration to remove a device through Home Assistant's integration-aware removal hook. Requires cap_integration_write plus an explicit WRITE grant on the device. config_entry_id is inferred only when the device has exactly one owner; multi-owner devices require it explicitly. Unsupported integrations and Phoenix MCP's own devices are refused before approval. The approval preview lists the selected owner's affected entities and known consumers, remaining owners, child devices at risk of losing their parent, permission references, and device-level MESA configuration. Removal is governed by the fully inherited MESA profile of exactly the affected entities. The integration may reject the request. This is destructive and cannot be restored from version history.
```

**{{ref:parameters}}**

```text
device_id: string  (required)
  The device registry id.
config_entry_id: string
  Owning config entry to remove. Optional only when exactly one owner exists.
```

**{{ref:example}}**

```json
{
  "name": "remove_device",
  "arguments": {
    "device_id": "8f3c1a2b4d5e6f708192a3b4c5d6e7f8"
  }
}
```

Captured in version history, but a deleted entry cannot be re-created through Phoenix MCP. Known relationship consumers are shown in the approval preview. Delete is governed by the entity's fully inherited MESA profile.
```

```

  }
}
```
blocks.get_radio_device:
- **{{ref:needs}}:** [{{label:caps.cap_diagnostics.label}}](guide:window.capabilities#diagnostics)
- **{{ref:hints}}:** {{ref:readOnly}} · {{ref:idempotent}}

**{{ref:description}}**

```text
Radio-level diagnostics for one device: signal quality (LQI/RSSI), availability, last seen, power source, interview state, and (ZHA backend) mesh neighbors. For Zigbee2MQTT devices it also returns bounded capability exposes plus converter-option definitions, effective values, and a content hash used by set_zigbee_device_options. Its radio_configuration also returns bounded endpoint, cluster, scoped binding, and configured-reporting state plus a conflict hash for binding/reporting tools. For Zigbee2MQTT, direct_property_fallback lists only readable exposes that MQTT discovery proves have no owning Home Assistant entity. Pass one listed property to read its current value and conflict hash. Prefer ordinary Home Assistant entities when a capability is represented there. device_id is Phoenix MCP's registry id from list_devices/get_device. The radio protocol and backend are detected automatically.
```

**{{ref:parameters}}**

```text
device_id: string  (required)
  Device registry ID to inspect.
property: string
  Optional property from direct_property_fallback.properties to read exactly.
```

**{{ref:example}}**

```json
{
  "name": "get_radio_device",
  "arguments": {
    "device_id": "8f3c1a2b4d5e6f708192a3b4c5d6e7f8"
  }
}
```
blocks.scan_zigbee_topology:
- **{{ref:needs}}:** [{{label:caps.cap_diagnostics.label}}](guide:window.capabilities#diagnostics), [{{label:caps.cap_radio_write.label}}](guide:window.capabilities#radio-write)
- **{{ref:hints}}:** {{ref:changes}}
- **{{ref:onConfirm}}:** {{ref:confirmApproval}}

**{{ref:description}}**

```text
Actively scan one ZHA or Zigbee2MQTT mesh and return a registry-scoped topology map. The result contains only accessible Home Assistant device IDs, one opaque coordinator node, directional neighbor links, LQI, and allowlisted relationship values. IEEE and network addresses, friendly names, routes, inaccessible nodes, hidden-node counts, and backend payloads are never returned. This query can make the Zigbee mesh less responsive for roughly 10 seconds to 2 minutes. Requires both Diagnostics and Radio Management and may require approval. When both backends exist, select one explicitly.
```

**{{ref:parameters}}**

```text
backend: "z2m" | "zha"
  Zigbee backend to scan; required only when both are present.
```

**{{ref:example}}**

```json
{
  "name": "scan_zigbee_topology",
  "arguments": {
    "backend": "zha"
  }
}
```

blocks.set_zigbee_device_options:
- **{{ref:needs}}:** [{{label:caps.cap_radio_write.label}}](guide:window.capabilities#radio-write)
- **{{ref:hints}}:** {{ref:changes}} · {{ref:destructive}} · {{ref:idempotent}}
- **{{ref:onConfirm}}:** {{ref:confirmApproval}}

**{{ref:description}}**

```text
Change Zigbee2MQTT converter options declared for one device. Read get_radio_device first and pass its options.content_hash as expected_hash. Only keys declared in options.definitions are accepted, and every value is validated against its type, enum, bounds, step, and nested structure. This does not write ordinary exposed control properties, accept MQTT topics or friendly names, or restart Zigbee2MQTT. Requires WRITE access to the device's entities and cap_radio_write, and may require admin confirmation. Zigbee2MQTT devices only.
```

**{{ref:parameters}}**

```text
device_id: string  (required)
  Zigbee2MQTT device registry ID to update.
options: object  (required)
  Non-empty partial map of converter-option property names to new values.
expected_hash: string  (required)
  Lowercase options.content_hash from the latest get_radio_device result.
```

**{{ref:example}}**

```json
{
  "name": "set_zigbee_device_options",
  "arguments": {
    "device_id": "8f3c1a2b4d5e6f708192a3b4c5d6e7f8",
    "options": {
      "temperature_precision": 1
    },
    "expected_hash": "3c2b1a0f9e8d7c6b"
  }
}
```
blocks.set_zigbee_device_property:
- **{{ref:needs}}:** [{{label:caps.cap_radio_write.label}}](guide:window.capabilities#radio-write), [{{label:caps.cap_physical_control.label}}](guide:window.capabilities#physical-control)
- **{{ref:hints}}:** {{ref:changes}} · {{ref:destructive}} · {{ref:idempotent}}
- **{{ref:onConfirm}}:** {{ref:confirmApproval}}

**{{ref:description}}**

```text
Directly change one readable/writable Zigbee2MQTT exposed property only when Home Assistant MQTT discovery proves no entity owns it. First call get_radio_device with property and pass property_read.content_hash as expected_hash. Values are validated against the converter expose definition and the device state must exactly confirm the result. Requires WRITE access to the device plus both cap_radio_write and cap_physical_control; either capability or MESA may require admin confirmation. No MQTT topic, friendly name, IEEE address, or arbitrary payload is caller-controlled.
```

**{{ref:parameters}}**

```text
device_id: string  (required)
  Zigbee2MQTT device registry ID to update.
property: string  (required)
  Property returned in direct_property_fallback.properties.
value: string | number | integer | boolean | object | array<any> | null  (required)
  New JSON value matching the property's exposed definition.
expected_hash: string  (required)
  Lowercase property_read.content_hash from the latest get_radio_device result.
```

**{{ref:example}}**

```json
{
  "name": "set_zigbee_device_property",
  "arguments": {
    "device_id": "8f3c1a2b4d5e6f708192a3b4c5d6e7f8",
    "property": "led_indicator",
    "value": false,
    "expected_hash": "6b5a4f3e2d1c0b9a"
  }
}
```
blocks.set_zigbee_binding:
- **{{ref:needs}}:** [{{label:caps.cap_radio_write.label}}](guide:window.capabilities#radio-write), [{{label:caps.cap_physical_control.label}}](guide:window.capabilities#physical-control)
- **{{ref:hints}}:** {{ref:changes}} · {{ref:destructive}} · {{ref:idempotent}}
- **{{ref:onConfirm}}:** {{ref:confirmApproval}}

**{{ref:description}}**

```text
Create or remove a direct device-to-device Zigbee binding. Both source and target are Home Assistant device registry IDs and must be WRITE-accessible on the same Zigbee network; callers never provide IEEE addresses or broker topics. For Zigbee2MQTT, first read both devices and pass explicit endpoint IDs, a non-empty cluster subset that is present as source-output and target-input, and both radio_configuration hashes. ZHA instead derives all compatible endpoints/clusters internally, so omit those Z2M-only fields. Requires both cap_radio_write and cap_physical_control plus inherited MESA evaluation across both devices, and may require confirmation. Unbinding preserves unrelated manual reporting configuration.
```

**{{ref:parameters}}**

```text
operation: "bind" | "unbind"  (required)
  Whether to create or remove the exact binding relationship.
source_device_id: string  (required)
  WRITE-accessible source Zigbee device registry ID.
target_device_id: string  (required)
  WRITE-accessible target Zigbee device registry ID on the same network.
source_endpoint: integer [1..254]
  Zigbee2MQTT source endpoint from get_radio_device; omit for ZHA.
target_endpoint: integer [1..254]
  Zigbee2MQTT target endpoint from get_radio_device; omit for ZHA.
clusters: array<string> [1..16 items]
  Zigbee2MQTT source-output/target-input cluster names; omit for ZHA.
expected_source_hash: string
  Zigbee2MQTT source radio_configuration.content_hash; omit for ZHA.
expected_target_hash: string
  Zigbee2MQTT target radio_configuration.content_hash; omit for ZHA.
```

**{{ref:example}}**

```json
{
  "name": "set_zigbee_binding",
  "arguments": {
    "operation": "bind",
    "source_device_id": "8f3c1a2b4d5e6f708192a3b4c5d6e7f8",
    "target_device_id": "1a2b3c4d5e6f708192a3b4c5d6e7f8a9b"
  }
}
```
blocks.configure_zigbee_reporting:
- **{{ref:needs}}:** [{{label:caps.cap_radio_write.label}}](guide:window.capabilities#radio-write)
- **{{ref:hints}}:** {{ref:changes}} · {{ref:destructive}} · {{ref:idempotent}}
- **{{ref:onConfirm}}:** {{ref:confirmApproval}}

**{{ref:description}}**

```text
Configure one Zigbee2MQTT attribute reporting record using an endpoint and input cluster listed by get_radio_device. Pass radio_configuration.content_hash to prevent races. Intervals are Zigbee seconds; maximum_report_interval 65535 disables reporting for the attribute. Short intervals can increase mesh traffic and battery use. Requires WRITE access and cap_radio_write, may require confirmation, and never accepts MQTT topics, friendly names, IEEE addresses, manufacturer options, or arbitrary payloads. For ZHA, use reconfigure_zigbee_device to re-apply integration-managed reporting.
```

**{{ref:parameters}}**

```text
device_id: string  (required)
  WRITE-accessible Zigbee2MQTT device registry ID.
endpoint: integer [1..254]  (required)
  Endpoint ID from radio_configuration.endpoints.
cluster: string  (required)
  Input cluster name listed for the selected endpoint.
attribute: string | integer  (required)
  Zigbee attribute name or numeric ID within the selected cluster.
minimum_report_interval: integer [0..65535]  (required)
  Minimum seconds between reports after a qualifying change.
maximum_report_interval: integer [0..65535]  (required)
  Maximum seconds between reports; 65535 disables reporting.
reportable_change: number [0..]
  Optional raw attribute change threshold; unit depends on the Zigbee attribute type.
expected_hash: string  (required)
  Lowercase radio_configuration.content_hash from the latest get_radio_device result.
```

**{{ref:example}}**

```json
{
  "name": "configure_zigbee_reporting",
  "arguments": {
    "device_id": "8f3c1a2b4d5e6f708192a3b4c5d6e7f8",
    "endpoint": 1,
    "cluster": "msTemperatureMeasurement",
    "attribute": "measuredValue",
    "minimum_report_interval": 30,
    "maximum_report_interval": 600,
    "reportable_change": 20,
    "expected_hash": "9a8b7c6d5e4f3a2b"
  }
}
```
blocks.create_zigbee_group:
- **{{ref:needs}}:** [{{label:caps.cap_radio_write.label}}](guide:window.capabilities#radio-write), [{{label:caps.cap_physical_control.label}}](guide:window.capabilities#physical-control)
- **{{ref:hints}}:** {{ref:changes}} · {{ref:destructive}} · {{ref:idempotent}}
- **{{ref:onConfirm}}:** {{ref:confirmApproval}}

**{{ref:description}}**

```text
Create one non-empty ZHA or Zigbee2MQTT group. The backend is inferred from 1 to 32 WRITE-accessible member device registry IDs; every endpoint must be listed by get_zigbee_groups.groupable_members, and all members must share one network. blocks.search_entities:
- **{{ref:needs}}:** [{{label:caps.cap_search.label}}](guide:window.capabilities#search)
- **{{ref:hints}}:** {{ref:readOnly}} · {{ref:idempotent}}

**{{ref:description}}**

```text
Search the entities this access key can access by name, domain, area, device_class, state, integration, or radio (zigbee, zwave, matter or bluetooth, read from the device registry). By default this searches live enabled entities. Set registry_state to disabled to find explicitly disabled registry entries, or all to also include enabled registry entries whose integration currently publishes no state. Registry-only access is inherited from the entity's device or domain. For semantic/profile-based discovery (tags, classification, control mode) use mesa_query_profiles instead. A multi-word query matches entities containing all the words (in entity_id, friendly_name, the entity's Assist aliases, or its area, floor, label, device name, manufacturer or model), and results are ranked by relevance so the best matches lead, name matches first; a row found through its area, floor, labels or device names them in matched. Filters combine with AND. Returns a compact list (entity_id, state, friendly_name, domain, area), with composed_name, the name Home Assistant now shows, when it differs from friendly_name and names no parent device the key cannot read; each result also carries control_mode when its MESA nature is non-default (read_only, confirm, prohibited), so you can spot restricted entities without a follow-up describe_entity call, entity_category (config or diagnostic) when the entity is a setup/health entity rather than a primary control, hidden true when it is hidden in Home Assistant's UI, and hint, the operator's note on what the entity is or how to use it, when one is set. total counts all scoped matching entities before paging; count is the number returned. When has_more is true, call again with offset set to next_offset for the next page. When the matches span several domains, by_domain counts all of them per domain. For counts alone (a total, or by_domain), use limit=1 to avoid enumerating the full list. To read the matching entities' current values too (a temperature with its unit, a thermostat's hvac_action), add projection exactly as get_state takes it, which saves a get_state call. To learn how the matching entities behaved over a period (which did not trigger this week), skip this listing: call get_history with mode summary and these filters as select, which finds and summarizes them in one call.
```

**{{ref:parameters}}**

```text
query: string
  Words matched against entity_id, friendly name and Assist aliases (case-insensitive).
domain: string | array<string>
  Restrict to one or more domains, e.g. light or [light, switch].
area: string
  An area id, name or alias, or a floor id, name or alias, which matches every area on that floor (case-insensitive).
has_area: boolean
  false finds entities with no area, directly or through their device; true only those with one.
device_class: string | array<string>
  One or more exact device_class values, e.g. motion or [door, window].
integration: string | array<string>
  One or more integrations that provide the entity, e.g. esphome or [hue, zha].
radio: "zigbee" | "zwave" | "matter" | "bluetooth" | array<("zigbee" | "zwave" | "matter" | "bluetooth")>
  Only entities whose device connects this way: zigbee (ZHA or Zigbee2MQTT), zwave, matter (Thread or Wi-Fi) or bluetooth.
power: "battery"
  battery: only entities whose device runs on a battery, shown by a diagnostic battery level or low-battery entity; phones and battery cameras count, a car's or home storage battery does not. Home Assistant records no mains or other power source.
state: string
  Exact current state value, e.g. on, off, home.
unavailable: boolean
  If true, only entities in state unavailable or unknown.
stale_hours: number
  Only entities unchanged for at least this many hours, by last_changed, which Home Assistant resets at every restart.
registry_state: "enabled" | "disabled" | "all"  (default "enabled")
  enabled searches live enabled entities; disabled searches explicitly disabled registry entries; all includes both plus enabled registry entries with no live state.
include_membership: boolean  (default false)
  Add is_group and visible direct member_entity_ids. Lists may be incomplete; hidden HA entities remain visible when permitted. is_group false means no valid explicit membership, not proof of a leaf; null means no live state or resource bounds prevented inspection. Discovery only, not execution or approval scope.
projection: object
  Optional, as in get_state: compact adds each live entity's key attributes, full all of its state, fields exact fields.
  kind: "compact" | "full" | "fields"  (required)
    Projection mode.
  fields: array<string>
    Exact fields, e.g. attr.unit_of_measurement or last_changed; only with kind fields.
limit: integer [1..500]  (default 100)
  Maximum matching entities to return.
offset: integer [0..]  (default 0)
  Number of ranked matches to skip; pass next_offset from the previous page.
```

**{{ref:example}}**

```json
{
  "name": "search_entities",
  "arguments": {
    "domain": "binary_sensor",
    "device_class": [
      "door",
      "window"
    ],
    "state": "on"
  }
}
```

Returns a job_id immediately; poll get_esphome_job to follow the compile and then the upload. Compiling finishing does NOT mean the device was flashed. If the device is currently offline the flash is armed for its next wake instead. Compile first with compile_esphome_firmware if you are not certain the config builds. If the upload is refused because the device did not offer OTA encryption, report that to the operator: never add allow_plaintext_upload or change a credential yourself to get the install through.
```

file: string  (required)

force_local: boolean

{

  "arguments": {
    "file": "living-room-sensor.yaml"
  }
}
```

While the job is still running you get only the most recent output, since that is what says where it has got to; the full build log comes back once it has finished. Poll every 30 seconds or so; a build normally takes several minutes. If you do not have the job_id, for example because it was started in an earlier conversation, pass file instead and the most recent job for that device is reported: use this to answer 'is that build done yet?'.
```

  Job lookup by job ID or device YAML file.

blocks.get_relationships:
- **{{ref:needs}}:** [{{label:caps.cap_search.label}}](guide:window.capabilities#search)
- **{{ref:hints}}:** {{ref:readOnly}} · {{ref:idempotent}}

**{{ref:description}}**

```text
Find what still USES a set of entities, before you change or remove anything. Pass one required scope object: kind entity, device, integration, area, or label plus its id, or a list of ids. Ask it the broadest way you can: 'what references this integration' is one call, and every helper type or every script is one list, where the same question per entity can be dozens. 'unreferenced' names the in-scope entities no searched consumer uses: candidates, not proof, since not_searched says what was not checked. Results are grouped by CONSUMER, each naming the in-scope entities it touches and their roles, so the response is the list of things you would have to edit. Combines Home Assistant's loaded reference graph with Phoenix's direct config scans, preserving detailed roles while adding package, blueprint, integration-managed, group, and person consumers. Covers automations, scripts, scenes, dashboards (with the card path, which patch_dashboard accepts directly), and config entries such as helpers built on another entity. 'searched' lists the consumer kinds actually checked and 'not_searched' names any unavailable, unreadable, unmodeled, or capability-skipped source, so a partial answer is marked incomplete. Only readable consumers are returned; hidden or unmapped identities are omitted. 'dangling_references' reports entity IDs referenced by something but no longer existing anywhere. With an entity scope it also returns 'references': what that automation or script itself uses; when configuration branches could not be read, 'references_not_searched' explains that this list is incomplete.
```

**{{ref:parameters}}**

```text
scope: object  (required)
  The one scope to inspect.
  kind: "entity" | "device" | "integration" | "area" | "label"  (required)
    Scope kind.
  id: string | array<string> [1.. items]  (required)
    Identifier for the selected scope, or a list of them.
```

**{{ref:example}}**

```json
{
  "name": "get_relationships",
  "arguments": {
    "scope": {
      "kind": "entity",
      "id": "sensor.old_power_meter"
    }
  }
}
```

If configuration branches could not be read, 'referenced_by_not_searched' explains why the reverse-reference list is incomplete. For full semantic profile data use mesa_get_profile (requires cap_config_read). 'not found' if not accessible.
```

**{{ref:parameters}}**

```text
entity_id: string  (required)
  The entity to describe.
```

**{{ref:example}}**

```json
{
  "name": "describe_entity",
  "arguments": {
    "entity_id": "climate.living_room"
  }
}
```

```

```text

  One or more entity IDs.
t1: string  (required)

t2: string
  Later time (ISO or relative). Defaults to now.
```

{

Use before repointing automations, scripts or dashboard cards from one entity to another: a narrowed min_temp/max_temp, a target_temp_step that only one side declares, or an option renamed between two integrations all break references that look correct. This is a snapshot of current attributes, not a history comparison (see compare_states for one entity over time, and get_history to compare values that vary).
```

**{{ref:parameters}}**

```text
entity_id: string  (required)
  The entity you have, e.g. the one being replaced.
compare_to: string  (required)
  The entity to compare it against, e.g. the replacement.
```

{

  }
}

{

  }
}

blocks.dry_run_service:

**{{ref:description}}**

```text

blocks.create_helper:
- **{{ref:needs}}:** [{{label:caps.cap_helper_write.label}}](guide:window.capabilities#helper-write)
- **{{ref:hints}}:** {{ref:changes}}
- **{{ref:onConfirm}}:** {{ref:confirmApproval}}

**{{ref:description}}**

```text
Create a Home Assistant helper. Storage helpers (input_boolean, input_number, input_text, input_select, input_datetime, input_button, counter, timer, schedule, zone, tag, person) use config. A helper integration that Home Assistant creates through a config flow, such as mold_indicator or history_stats, uses cumulative flow_steps instead: start with [] to receive its first real form or supported menu, then append each {step_id, data} and call again. Fields carry Home Assistant's own help text. A rejected step returns that form with its errors: replace that step's data rather than appending. Template creation starts with {step_id: 'user', data: {next_step_id: '<listed type>'}}, followed by the returned final form. Every supported Template type offered by this Home Assistant release is listed. Incomplete flows are closed without creating anything; the final form is approval-gated. Creating a zone requires write access to its entire entity domain so the new entity remains manageable. Person creation similarly requires person-domain write plus write access to every proposed device tracker; only name and device_trackers are accepted, never a raw Home Assistant user id or picture. Tag creation requires tag_id and accepts only name/description metadata; scan history cannot be forged. Inherited MESA applies to the proposed helper and is rechecked after materialization; a new entity that resolves more restrictively than the approved proposal is removed. OTP is excluded.
```

**{{ref:parameters}}**

```text
helper_type: string  (required)
  Helper domain, such as input_boolean, mold_indicator, or history_stats.
config: object
  Storage-helper fields; do not use with flow_steps. Keys by type: input_boolean name, icon, initial; input_number name, min, max (both required), step, mode (slider|box), unit_of_measurement, initial; input_text name, min, max, pattern, mode (text|password), initial; input_select name, options (required list), initial; input_datetime name, has_date and/or has_time, initial; input_button name; counter name, initial, step, minimum, maximum, restore; timer name, duration (HH:MM:SS), restore; schedule name plus monday..sunday lists of {from, to}. Every type except tag and person accepts icon. Setting initial makes the helper start at that value after every restart instead of restoring its last state.
flow_steps: array<object> [..8 items]
  Cumulative config-flow steps. Use [] to inspect the first form or supported menu; resend prior steps plus the next step on each call. Menu data contains only next_step_id.
  each item:
    step_id: string  (required)
      Step ID returned by the helper config flow.
    data: object  (required)
      Returned form fields, or next_step_id for a menu choice.
```

**{{ref:example}}**

```json
{
  "name": "create_helper",
  "arguments": {
    "helper_type": "input_boolean",
    "config": {
      "name": "Guest mode",
      "icon": "mdi:account-multiple"
    }
  }
}
```
blocks.edit_helper:
- **{{ref:needs}}:** [{{label:caps.cap_helper_write.label}}](guide:window.capabilities#helper-write)

**{{ref:description}}**

```text
Update an existing helper's config by its helper_type and helper_id. Send only the fields to change: every other stored field keeps its current value, and null clears an optional field. For Template helpers, list_helpers reports the entity domain as helper_type; config contains settings-flow values and is checked against the entry's live options schema. Omitted options are preserved by Home Assistant's options flow. A verified Template helper edit includes a recovery_id. Inherited MESA is resolved before approval and fingerprint-rechecked at execution. Zone, tag, and person edits require write access to that storage entity and reject unknown fields. Person edits accept only name/device_trackers, require write access to every current and proposed tracker, and preserve private user/picture bindings. Tags expose only name and description; scan history is read-only. A zone's icon can be replaced but not removed.
```

**{{ref:parameters}}**

```text
helper_type: string  (required)
  Helper domain, such as input_boolean, counter, timer, zone, tag, or person.
helper_id: string  (required)
  The helper id (from list_helpers).
config: object  (required)
  Fields to change, e.g. {"icon": "mdi:sofa"}. Omitted fields keep their current values; null clears an optional field.
```

**{{ref:example}}**

```json
{
  "name": "edit_helper",
  "arguments": {
    "helper_type": "input_boolean",
    "helper_id": "guest_mode",
    "config": {
      "icon": "mdi:sofa"
    }
  }
}
```

Zone, tag, and person deletion require write access to that storage-backed entity; person deletion also requires write access to every linked tracker. Scanning a deleted physical tag can make Home Assistant discover it again.
```

**{{ref:parameters}}**

- **{{ref:needsOne}}:** [{{label:caps.cap_helper_write.label}}](guide:window.capabilities#helper-write), [{{label:caps.cap_blueprint_write.label}}](guide:window.capabilities#blueprint-write), [{{label:caps.cap_energy_write.label}}](guide:window.capabilities#energy-write), [{{label:caps.cap_lovelace_write.label}}](guide:window.capabilities#lovelace-write), [{{label:caps.cap_dashboard_resources.label}}](guide:window.capabilities#dashboard-resources)
- **{{ref:hints}}:** {{ref:changes}} · {{ref:destructive}} · {{ref:idempotent}}
- **{{ref:onConfirm}}:** {{ref:confirmApproval}}

**{{ref:description}}**

```text
Restore a secret-safe Template helper, blueprint, Energy, or dashboard registry/layout/resource snapshot created by this access key. First send recovery_id and side to get a snapshot digest and current-target fingerprint; resend both values to request normal family-capability approval. The executor rechecks current authority and the target, then uses that family's Home Assistant API and verifies readback. A blueprint comes back as Home Assistant re-renders it, without its comments or formatting; the receipt says so when that changes the text. A registry snapshot from before the dashboard existed deletes it with its views, after saving a layout copy. Unsupported families and non-invertible effects are refused.
```

**{{ref:parameters}}**

```text
recovery_id: string  (required)
  Recovery record ID returned by an earlier write.
side: "before" | "source"  (required)
  Snapshot side to restore.
snapshot_digest: string
  Digest from the restore receipt; required on the approval request.
target_fingerprint: string
  Current-target fingerprint from the restore receipt; required on the approval request.
```

**{{ref:example}}**

```json
{
  "name": "restore_configuration",
  "arguments": {
    "recovery_id": "rcv_01JD4M2N3B4V5C6X7Z8A9S0D1F",
    "side": "before"
  }
}
```

- **{{ref:needs}}:** [{{label:caps.cap_yaml_edit.label}}](guide:window.capabilities#yaml-edit)
- **{{ref:hints}}:** {{ref:readOnly}} · {{ref:idempotent}}

**{{ref:description}}**

```text
Read a YAML configuration file, or one key inside it. With no arguments this returns configuration.yaml. Pass file to read another YAML file in the configuration directory (an !include target such as automations.yaml or packages/kitchen.yaml), and key to return just that top-level or nested mapping key instead of the whole file. The text is as written except that a value under a credential-named key, a credential inside a URL or other value, and a comment naming one show as <redacted>, so that is not the file's real value. Masking works by name, so a secret under an ordinary name stays visible. !include and !secret are returned as written, never resolved. A file that does not parse is refused, as its credentials cannot be located; the error gives the line. Files with secret in their name, hidden directories, the esphome directory and paths with characters outside printable ASCII cannot be read. Use get_esphome_yaml for ESPHome device files, where entity scope is enforced. content_hash covers the WHOLE file, even when key is given, and is only comparable between reads. This tool only reads: YAML configuration is edited by the operator, and automations, scripts and scenes are changed with their own tools.

- **{{ref:needs}}:** [{{label:caps.cap_helper_write.label}}](guide:window.capabilities#helper-write)

```text
Read a HELPER's settings and the schema for changing them. Helpers are the entries Home Assistant classifies as helpers: threshold, derivative, switch_as_x, min_max, utility_meter, attribute-as-sensor and similar, the ones built ON another entity. Find the entry_id with get_relationships (a helper shows up as a config_entry consumer of the entity it uses) or list_integrations. Returns the current options, a content_hash to pass back as expected_hash, and schema: the fields the helper accepts with their types, defaults, Home Assistant's help text and, for entity fields, the domains they allow. editable_settings is the subset of the current settings the flow actually offers, and is what you send back to set_helper_settings: a helper often stores keys its flow does not expose, and sending one of those is rejected. mechanism says which flow the helper uses (options or reconfigure); both are driven the same way from your side. Integration entries are not readable here.
```

```text
entry_id: string  (required)
  The config entry id of the helper.
```

{

  "arguments": {
    "entry_id": "01JD4K7Z8Q2W3E4R5T6Y7U8I9O"
  }
}
```

- **{{ref:needs}}:** [{{label:caps.cap_helper_write.label}}](guide:window.capabilities#helper-write)

```text

This is what finishes a migration: a helper whose source is gone keeps existing and quietly produces nothing, and no other tool can repoint it. Read get_helper_settings first and send back its editable_settings with your change applied, NOT the full settings: your input is merged over the form's current suggested values. Omitted fields retain those values; a key the flow does not offer is rejected if you send it. To clear an optional field with no default, explicitly send null; other fields follow the form's validation. Pass that read's content_hash as expected_hash so the write is refused if something else changed the settings meanwhile. Any entity you name must be one this access key could already control. May require admin approval. Inherited MESA is resolved across every entity owned by the helper and fingerprint-rechecked before its flow runs. The helper reloads with the new settings; no restart. Helpers only, and a helper whose options flow has more than one step must be changed in the Home Assistant UI.
```

**{{ref:parameters}}**

```text
entry_id: string  (required)
  The config entry id of the helper.
settings: object  (required)
  The new settings, matching the schema from get_helper_settings. Send its editable_settings with your change applied.
expected_hash: string
  Optional. The content_hash from a prior get_helper_settings; the write is refused if the settings changed since then.
```

**{{ref:example}}**

```json
{
  "name": "set_helper_settings",
  "arguments": {
    "entry_id": "01JD4K7Z8Q2W3E4R5T6Y7U8I9O",
    "settings": {
      "entity_id": "sensor.new_power_meter"

    "expected_hash": "5e4d3c2b1a098f7e"
  }
}
```

```text

**{{ref:description}}**

```text
Change path-addressed values anywhere in a Lovelace dashboard without resending the layout. Adding or changing a template, a custom: card or an absolute URL always needs approval. Read the whole layout only for something search cannot find, such as a view option. Each change's path is an array of keys and 0-based indexes, e.g. ["views", 0, "badges", 4, "entity"]; kind set replaces or adds the value there, append adds to a list it addresses, remove deletes it. Changes apply in order, each to the layout the previous one left, and all of them or none are written, under one approval. Nothing is created along the way, so a path whose parent does not exist is refused rather than built. Omit target.url_path for the default dashboard. Storage-mode dashboards only. Pass expected_hash to refuse the write if the layout changed since your read. A successful result confirms the change and returns the new content_hash; do not re-read to check it. Values a read redacted are refused: writing the placeholder back would overwrite real configuration.
```

  url_path: string

```

  "arguments": {

          "sections",
          1,
          "cards",
          2,
          "entity"
